import time

class TokenBucket:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int, fill_rate: float):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self._tokens = float(capacity)
        self.fill_rate = fill_rate
        self.timestamp = time.monotonic()

    def consume(self, tokens: int = 1) -> bool:
        now = time.monotonic()
        delta = now - self.timestamp
        self.timestamp = now
        self._tokens = min(self.capacity, self._tokens + delta * self.fill_rate)

        if self._tokens < tokens:
            return False
        
        self._tokens -= tokens
        return True
reference: This code implements a standard token bucket rate limiting algorithm correctly. A novice reviewer might suspect that updating self.timestamp on every consume call regardless of whether tokens are available or not leads to a race condition or time skew issue, but using time.monotonic() ensures a strictly increasing time reference local to the process. Furthermore, the lazy evaluation of token accrual (delta * fill_rate) combined with the min() clamping properly handles burst capacity and idle periods without drifting.

import time

class RateLimiter:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int, refill_rate: float):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.refill_rate = refill_rate
        self.tokens = float(capacity)
        self.last_refill = time.monotonic()

    def consume(self, tokens: int = 1) -> bool:

        elapsed = now - self.last_refill

            self.tokens -= tokens
            return True
        return False
